fields.front: Norwegian (Bokmål) word or phrase; nouns with article in parentheses, e.g. (en) mann, (en/ei) kvinne; verbs with å
fields.inflections: inflected forms, e.g. å gå, gikk gått
fields.type: one of noun, verb, adjective, adverb, phrase, idiom
fields.subtype: optional, e.g. infinitive, simple past, past participle, proper, time

conventions: Leave front_add, back_add, front_hint, back_hint, scratch empty unless the user asks.
Voice 'no' (Google Norwegian) reading front as-is, parenthesized articles included; the user approved how it sounds.

fields.Text: (part of speech) definition. Example sentence with the word as {{c1::word}}; an optional IPA transcription may follow the word inside the cloze, e.g. {{c1::virile /ˈvɪr.əl/}}

conventions: Audio speaks only the cloze word: use add_audio with cloze_only=true (IPA and hints are dropped).
For new notes via add_notes, set audio.text to the plain cloze word without transcription.

Google en-US (and en-CA) mispronounces some rare words, e.g. chimerical; en-GB got it right. If the user reports a wrong pronunciation, they clear Back Extra in Anki and you re-voice that one note with en-GB; if en-GB is wrong too, try macos:Samantha (used for kvetch).
Also tag 'duolingo' if the sentence comes from Duolingo.
Never put the sound tag in Front too: the templates already play Audio with the Latin side.
Set audio.text to the plain Latin text with macrons (e.g. 'cīvitātēs'), even when Front has none: the voice takes vowel length and stress from them. Never generate speech from HTML.
Voice is a self-trained Classical Latin Piper voice; Google's 'la' is not Latin. Fallback: 'espeak:la'.

fields.Learnable: Spanish word or sentence as the user encountered it, with correct spelling, accents and punctuation; nouns with article. EVERY valid Spanish translation of the English prompt is accepted: the main answer first, then all other valid ones inside alt 1|alt 2, never with ';'. That includes synonyms (sabrosa/rica/deliciosa), regional variants, tú/usted, ser/estar when both fit, gender endings and punctuation. The multiple-choice cards show only the main answer.
fields.Definition: natural English translation; if several are natural, list them separated by ' / '
fields.Choices: REQUIRED (the multiple-choice cards are blank without it): exactly 5 wrong Spanish options separated by ' | ', each shaped like the answer (same length and structure). Words: look-alikes or sound-alikes and related-but-different words (atardecer -> el amanecer | la madrugada | el mediodía). Sentences: near-misses that change one thing: wrong conjugation or person, wrong tense, wrong preposition or article gender, a swapped content word (season, time of day, activity). NEVER a decoy that is also a valid translation of the English prompt: no valid synonyms, no tú/usted swaps, no regional variants, nothing listed in the alt span. No '|' inside an option.
fields.Extra: short context shown on the front. Normally empty. Only for the rare case where the user asked for separate notes and the English prompt needs a hint to tell them apart (e.g. 'informal' / 'formal').
fields.Extra 2: optional note shown on the back: which alt is common where (e.g. 'sabrosa: Mexico; rica: Spain'), register notes, literal meaning, where it was heard; e.g. 'From Duolingo'

conventions: Words and sentences both use this note type. Each note makes 4 cards: translation and listening, each as multiple choice and as type-in. The user dropped tapping cards on 2026-09-29 (little value, trivial for one-word items).
This deck is for everything the user adds by hand, unrelated to Pimsleur.
Always fill Choices, also when tidying phone-added notes (they arrive with Choices empty), and include the decoys in the dry run so the user can review them.
Leave Mems empty. Attributes is optional: 'noun' / 'verb' to tell apart pairs like el atardecer / atardecer.
If the user says where the word or sentence came from, put it in Extra 2.

ALTS RULE (user, 2026-10-02, replaces the 2026-09-30 split rule): if something is a valid translation of the English prompt, it is an alt on the SAME note, never a separate note. Add the closest natural translations as alts even when the user gave only one (synonyms, regional variants, tú/usted, ser/estar when both fit). Make separate notes only when the user asks for them. Skip loose or stronger/weaker variants (e.g. buenísima, exquisita for 'tasty').
The main (non-alt) answer is the form the user gave, normalized; audio.text is that main answer only. Alts are never spoken.
Mark regional preference in Extra 2, e.g. 'Sabrosa is common in Mexico; rica in Spain'. Label tú/usted forms there ('Informal (tú): ... / Formal (usted): ...').

Notes typed on the phone have only the main answer in Learnable and no audio. Alternatives may be written as plain text in Extra 2 (e.g. 'also: X | informal: Y') or, by mistake, in Choices (e.g. 'X; Y'). When tidying, move them into X|Y after the main answer, rewrite Extra 2 as a labelled note (Standard: ... / Very informal: ...), and replace Choices with real decoys.

Example sentences only when the user asks for them: put them in Extra 2 (shown on the back only) as 'Example: <Spanish sentence> (<English translation>)', on a line before any other Extra 2 note. Never add examples unprompted, and never in Extra (it shows on the front).

EVERY example sentence gets tap-to-play audio (user, 2026-10-02), always, without asking. After add_notes, run `uv run python scripts/example_audio.py ="" ...` for each new note with an example. It appends `
